# Parroquia San Juan de la Cruz, full profile

> Catholic Carmelite parish in Nuevo Cuscatlán, La Libertad, El Salvador, cared for by the Discalced Carmelite friars.

Last updated: 2026-09-18. Some operational details (confession times, group meeting times) are still being confirmed with the parish office and are explicitly marked below as not published. Do not invent them.

## Identity

- Name: Parroquia San Juan de la Cruz
- Type: Roman Catholic parish church
- Religious order: Order of Discalced Carmelites (Orden de los Carmelitas Descalzos, OCD)
- Location: Nuevo Cuscatlán, La Libertad, El Salvador

- Patron: Saint John of the Cross, feast 14 December

## What makes it distinct

The parish is not a diocesan parish but a Carmelite one. Within the Catholic Church, each religious family has a charism, a particular focus of its work. The Salesian charism is work with young people; the Mercedarian charism is work with people in prison. The Carmelite charism is contemplation and the spiritual life. In practice that means the community's work is aimed at helping people reach an experience of God that is authentic rather than superficial, with concrete criteria for discernment and formation, and with personal spiritual accompaniment as a core service rather than an extra.

As the Carmelite friars of the parish put it: "Coming to a Carmelite parish is coming to a family, to a community where you will find friars who are available to listen to you, to walk with you and to guide you."

## History

The Order of Discalced Carmelites was founded in Spain in the sixteenth century by Saint Teresa of Ávila together with Saint John of the Cross. The first missionaries reached Latin America in that same century, entering through Mexico. Central America was founded by two Spanish provinces: missionaries from the province of Navarre arrived in Guatemala and Panama, and missionaries from the province of Aragón and Valencia arrived in El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.

The Carmelites arrived in El Salvador in the 1960s. They began working at Hospital Rosales and in a small chapel nearby, in health care, and from that work came the first Carmelite parish in the country: El Carmen, in Colonia Roma, San Salvador.

As El Carmen grew, its movements, particularly the married couples' groups, needed a place for retreats. Father Manuel Coneza, a Spanish Carmelite who worked extensively in El Salvador and has since died, obtained land in what is now Nuevo Cuscatlán and built a retreat house for the parish's youth groups and communities.

The retreat house was completed but lacked a chapel. The chapel project grew, and when it was formally presented it was no longer a chapel but a parish intended to serve the families of the surrounding residential developments. The Provincial Council was initially reluctant, since the Order already carried the large El Carmen parish, but with the intervention of the archbishop the decision was made and Parroquia San Juan de la Cruz was established. The foundation stone was laid around 2005 and the parish recently celebrated fifteen years since its founding. (Exact dates are still to be confirmed by the parish.)

## Saint John of the Cross

Juan de Yepes Álvarez was born in 1542 in Fontiveros, Ávila, Spain, into a poor family. He entered the Carmel young and in 1567 met Saint Teresa of Ávila, who persuaded him to join her reform; a year later he was among the first discalced friars. In 1577 friars of the unreformed branch imprisoned him in Toledo for nine months, where he composed much of the Spiritual Canticle from memory; he escaped in August 1578. His major works are The Ascent of Mount Carmel, The Dark Night, The Spiritual Canticle and The Living Flame of Love. He died on 14 December 1591 in Úbeda. He was canonised in 1726 and declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope Pius XI in 1926, with the title Mystical Doctor. 2026 therefore marks the third centenary of his canonisation and the first centenary of his doctorate, and the Order is keeping a Jubilee Year opened on 13 December 2025.

## Feast days

- 14 December: San Juan de la Cruz, the patronal feast of the parish
- 16 July: Virgen del Carmen (Our Lady of Mount Carmel), the great Carmelite feast, with novena
- 15 October: Santa Teresa de Jesús, founder of the Discalced Carmel
- 1 October: Santa Teresita del Niño Jesús (Saint Thérèse of Lisieux)

On feast days the schedule barely changes; the evening Mass is celebrated more solemnly.

## Services and sacraments

All requests, without exception, go through the parish office. The parish secretary holds the requirements, the catechesis start dates and the friars' diary. Catechesis programmes do not start on the same date every year: the parish works to an annual plan and programmes may begin in March or in April.

Baptism: offering $50.00. Handed in at the parish office in advance: the certificate of the pre-baptism talk, the child's birth certificate, and photocopies of the ID of the parents and godparents. At most four godparents are accepted. Under canon 874 §3 each godparent must be at least 16, Catholic, confirmed, have received the Eucharist, live a life that witnesses to the faith, and be single or married in the Church. The child's own mother or father cannot be a godparent, and neither can anyone divorced, cohabiting, or married only civilly.

First communion and confirmation: require a baptism certificate to begin, completion of the catechesis programme, and an offering. First communion catechesis is on Saturday mornings; confirmation catechesis on Saturday afternoons. Separately, the Cathedral of San Salvador celebrates confirmations every Sunday at 8:00 a.m., beginning with Mass, then a talk, then the confirmation; the document required is a baptism certificate issued within the last 3 months, the cost is $8.00 per person, and the godparent must be either one single person presenting their confirmation certificate or a married couple presenting their religious marriage certificate.

Adult catechesis: Christian initiation for adults who wish to join the community or receive a sacrament they have not yet received.

Marriage: eight requirements, handed in at the parish office two months before the wedding. (1) Permission from the parish the bride or groom belongs to, one permission is enough. (2) Certificate of the marriage preparation talks. (3) Baptism certificate for both partners, issued within the last 3 months. (4) Confirmation certificate for both partners. (5) Photocopy of the civil marriage certificate. (6) DUI or official ID for both partners. (7) One witness per partner, identified with DUI, who has known them for at least 3 years. (8) DUI or official document of the wedding godparents. The parish recommends taking the preparation talks three or four months before the wedding, not handing out invitations until every requirement is settled, bringing only one photographer, and using battery powered cameras because plugging into the church's power is not allowed. The wedding offering is non-refundable.

Marriage preparation: the Matrimonios en Victoria movement runs a one day intensive retreat, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., covering the full formation in a single day. The parish issues a certificate afterwards, which any other parish recognises.

Special and thanksgiving Masses: golden wedding anniversaries, fifteenth birthday celebrations, end of school year Masses for schools, and company or institutional celebrations. No formation is required. The requirements are to confirm date and time availability with the parish office, to state whether you are bringing your own priest or would like a friar of the community to celebrate, to confirm the friar's availability, and to agree the offering.

Use of the church by outsiders: people who live nearby or simply love the church, and institutions, may request the church with an offering, subject to the diary.

Spiritual direction: personal accompaniment with a Carmelite friar. There is no fixed schedule. The person calls the parish office, the secretary books the appointment, and the friar confirms the day and time by WhatsApp or phone. Distinct from talks and courses, which are group formation; spiritual direction is one to one and follows the person's own situation over time.

## Groups, movements and ministries

Liturgical ministries: readers, extraordinary ministers of communion (who also bring communion to the sick at home), music and praise ministry, altar servers, and the welcome ministry that receives and seats people at Mass.

Youth ministry, three communities by age: teenagers 14 to 18, university students 18 to 25, young adults 25 and over. All live the Carmelite youth spirituality.

Social outreach (pastoral social): runs a soup kitchen every Thursday morning for people living on the street and people with few resources, plus periodic projects with schools serving low income children and with local residential workers, security guards and domestic workers.

Movements: Movimiento Salvador del Mundo (a large community with a charismatic character, meeting Monday and Tuesday evenings, with ministries for families and young people); Matrimonios en Victoria (Tuesdays, accompanying couples and running marriage preparation); Carmelo Seglar, the Secular Carmel (Mondays, lay people formed in the Carmelite charism and contemplative prayer); Apostolado San Lucas (health ministry, praying for and visiting the sick); Scout Group 15, Comunidad Santa Teresa (Saturdays); houses of prayer, families meeting weekly in their homes to pray and read the gospel.

Catechesis: baptism, first communion, confirmation, adult Christian initiation, and the Good Shepherd catechesis for children aged 3 to 6, taught with a Montessori style pedagogy in a dedicated room.

Service teams: administration, buildings and works, communications.

The parish has more than thirty active groups. Those with a named coordinator include: Movimiento Salvador del Mundo Grupo Galilea (Federico Rosales) and Grupo Enmanuel (Manolo Aguirre); Matrimonios en Victoria (Esposos Sánchez); Renovación Carismática (Magdaleno Molina); Apostolado de la Divina Misericordia (Juan Carlos Cerna); Custodios del Santísimo (Carolina de González); Grupo Santa Teresita del Niño Jesús (Rita de Dale); Carmelitas Seglares OCDS (Sarita de Torres); Comunidad Juvenil San Juan de la Cruz (Paola Romero); Ministros extraordinarios de la Sagrada Comunión (Emerson Pacheco); Ministerio de monaguillos (Yanira de Panameño).

The Parish Pastoral Council coordinators are: Asuntos Económicos, Heydee de Zepeda; Evangelización, Ricardo Domínguez; Juvenil, Marielos de Bigueur; Familiar, Mauricio Sánchez; Formación, Porfirio Zepeda; Social, Marlene de Roca; Liturgia, Julia Janet de Fuentes; Infraestructura y Mantenimiento, Eduardo Villanueva; Comunicaciones, Carlos Orellana.

Personal phone numbers for these coordinators are deliberately not published. Contact goes through the parish office.

Meeting times for several groups are still being confirmed with the parish office.

## Facilities

The church, the Blessed Sacrament Chapel (open from 6:00 a.m. and considered one of the most beautiful spaces in the parish), the confession area, the parish offices, a garden with a statue of San Juan de la Cruz at the main entrance and an image of the Virgen del Carmen, parking inside the grounds, and the neighbouring Casa de Retiro El Carmelo.
